title: “Decí por qué no querés” by Palito Ortega
text: Ramón Bautista Ortega is an Argentine singer and actor, better known as Palito Ortega (pronounced ). Ortega is an icon of Argentine popular music, and is considered one of the main representatives of the musical style called New wave that marked the Hispanic-American music between the years '60 and '70.
listen: Decí por qué no querés Palito Ortega

title: “¡Oh, mi señor!” by Edoardo Vianello
text: Edoardo Vianello is an Italian singer, composer and actor, considered one of the most popular Italian singers of the 1960s.

title: “Dominique” by Sor Sonrisa/Los Alegres Cantores
text: Dominique is a 1963 French-language popular song, written and performed by Belgian singer Jeanne-Paule Marie Deckers, better known as "Sœur Sourire" or "The Singing Nun". The song is about Saint Dominic, a Spanish-born religious priest and founder of the Order of Preachers, of which Deckers was a member.

title: “¡Qué suerte!” by Violeta Rivas/Los Tres Sudamericanos/ Beto Fernán
text: Ana María Francisca Adinolfi was an Argentine singer and actress, known for participating in the music program El Club del Clan, along with Palito Ortega, Raúl Lavié, Johnny Tedesco and Chico Novarro.
listen: ¡Qué suerte! Violeta Rivas/Los Tres Sudamericanos/ Beto Fernán

title: “Cómo te extraño, mi amor” by Leo Dan
text: Leopoldo Dante Tévez was an Argentine composer and singer. He recorded more than 20 albums during his long career during the late 20th century between Argentina and Mexico.
listen: Cómo te extraño, mi amor Leo Dan

title: “Twist and Shout” by The Beatles/Los Tammys
text: "Twist and Shout" is a 1961 song written by Phil Medley and Bert Berns. It was originally recorded by The Top Notes, but it did not become a hit in the record charts until it was reworked by the Isley Brothers for their album Twist & Shout in 1962.
listen: Twist and Shout The Beatles/Los Tammys

title: “Chin, chin” by Richard Anthony/Violeta Rivas
text: Richard Anthony was an Egyptian-born French pop singer who had his greatest success in the 1960s and 1970s.

title: “Collar de caracolas” by Julio Molina Cabral/Luis Ordóñez/ Los Fronterizos
text: Los Fronterizos is an Argentine musical band consisting of four men. The group was established in 1953 in the northern province of Salta -- bordering on Bolivia -- from which "Los Fronterizos" is derived.
listen: Collar de caracolas Julio Molina Cabral/Luis Ordóñez/ Los Fronterizos

title: “A Hard Day's Night” by The Beatles
text: "A Hard Day's Night" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles. Credited to Lennon–McCartney, it was primarily written by John Lennon, with some minor collaboration from Paul McCartney.
listen: A Hard Day's Night The Beatles
